context:
Goal: the batch gate is as short as it can be once the Linux splits and your macOS ruling (R61) land.
Problem (goal): after those land, the Windows job checks-windows-rest is the longest gate job at about 31 minutes, so every batch still waits about 32 minutes.
Based on (measured): checks-windows-rest took 31.7 and 30.1 minutes on two batch PR runs; most of it is Windows starting processes (274 seconds of guard wrappers on Windows against 28 on Linux).
Based on (measured): the touched-tests job ran 1288 times in 24 hours, each fetching full history for 19 to 30 seconds.
Departs from: main runs checks-windows-rest as one job and fetches full history for touched-tests — the job splits into 2 or 3 parallel jobs and touched-tests fetches only recent history.

options.gain: The gate drops from about 32 to about 16 minutes, and about 430 Linux minutes a day leave drafts.
options.how: checks-windows-rest runs as 2 or 3 jobs side by side, and touched-tests fetches only recent history.
options.label: Split the job and fetch less history (Recommended)
options.lose: No coverage lost; the split works around slow Windows process starts rather than fixing them.

options.gain: Each suite runs once per batch, about 290 runner minutes saved per batch.
options.how: As a, plus the push-to-main run is skipped when its files equal the green batch PR head (8 of 8 merges matched), with the full Windows shards moved into the PR run.
options.label: a, and skip the main run when it matches the batch
options.lose: No check of each commit on main; your macOS nightly skip and the red-main gate read main runs and need rework; no speed gain, since Linux and Windows never queue.

options.gain: About 60 Windows minutes saved per batch.
options.how: As a, plus the full Windows guard shards stop running on the push to main, and one mutation test runs on Linux only.
options.label: a, and drop the full Windows guard shards on main
options.lose: Guard cases not tagged for Windows are no longer checked on Windows.

options.label: Keep as is
options.lose: Each batch keeps waiting about 32 minutes on one Windows job.

ref: retrospective 15:53 CST Nov 12, Linux and Windows CI audit (runs 43288661492, 43234925158)
reply: Closed 16:03 CST: you answered in the retrospective's chat at 15:55 CST (ruling R62): split the Windows job and fetch less history (a), and skip the main run when it matches the batch (b); dropping the full Windows shards (c) is held, since b keeps them once per batch. Lane ci-linux-windows-once does it.
short: Shorter batch gate after the macOS cuts
title: Split the longest Windows check job and fetch less history for touched-tests
why: Each option trades CI time against coverage on main, which is your call.
